title: THE DEACON KNOCKS BACK (FULL WAKE)
description: The definitive Velvet Hearse production: THE VELVET HEARSE, "The Deacon Is Dead" (1972, imaginary), the approved short version THE DEACON KNOCKS BACK sampled as a second record, and fragments of it reversed. Seven equal steps, 96 BPM; a conversation between the living and the dead.

tracks.description: gen 1: Lucius's likembe alone, the bed.
gen 1: Iggy's knocks on the lid, an octave up; as calls, as a triad, as the seven-step scale, in the exchange.
gen 1: the Deacon from inside: the reply (rate 0.552, the tonic an octave down), his knocks as recorded, the dead kick of the argument.
gen 1: the Deacon's knocks from inside as recorded, and the argument's dead kick between its accents; lightly driven (R3).
gen 1: the urn, one palm thud.
gen 1: the bead slap and tap, laid back.
gen 1: one shake of the collection plate.
gen 1: the hearse spring tried once on A1, played in seven steps with glides.
gen 1: the record as found: Odile, the stairs whole, halved and doubled, the two stabs, the hot shout, the last bar.
gen 1: the door opening, lifting, closing.
gen 2: the short version's wake heard through the coffin lid.
gen 2: the short version cut into sixteenths and dealt out again; its seven-knock scale stacked; its laugh.
gen 3: the other side: the reply, the knocks and the scale from the short version, backwards.
